title: The Balance Sheet
lede: Donald Trump says he takes no presidential salary. This page sets that salary beside what he and his family are documented to have received during the term, with every figure traced to its source.
description: The presidential salary Donald Trump says he does not take, set beside the income, paper value and settlements documented for him and his family during the term. Every figure is sourced.

sections.title: Salary
intro: The salary is set by law. What has been done with it is documented only in part.

items.text: Trump has said repeatedly during the term that he does not keep the salary. On 29 Sep 2026 he said: 'I don't take my salary ... I decided not to, including in my first term.' These are his statements, not records of payment.
One recipient: the White House Historical Association, a private nonprofit. Its statement of 27 Oct 2025 credits him with $66,000 of salary since January. About $306,800 had accrued by that date.

No donation is documented for any period after Oct 2025. The White House has published no quarterly announcements, as it did from 2017 to 2020. A gap in announcements is not proof that no donation was made.

3 U.S.C. 102 sets the salary at $400,000 a year, paid monthly, plus a $50,000 expense allowance for official duties. Any unused part of the allowance reverts to the Treasury. At that rate $725,000 to $730,000 of salary had accrued by 16 Nov 2026.
A donated salary can be claimed as a charitable deduction. No tax return for the second term is public, so whether one was claimed is unknown.

items.text: The disclosure reports gross receipts. It states no costs, taxes or profit.
Three crypto lines sit on entities 30% held by 'Trump Family Members', and twelve licensing companies are 20% held by them. The form does not say whether an amount is the entity's total or his share.
Not yet disclosed. The report covering 2026 is due in May 2027.

Income received during the presidency is not shown to be income received because of it. The clubs, rents, books and pensions predate the term. Nothing on this page shows that money was received in exchange for an official act.
Paper value is not cash. Share and token values move daily, and no sale is reported for the holdings listed.
A gap in announcements is not proof that no donation was made, and a statement of intent is not proof that one was.
Neither the President nor his family has ever engaged, or will ever engage, in conflicts of interest.
At nearly 1,000 pages, it represents one of the most comprehensive financial disclosure reports ever submitted and demonstrates a level of financial transparency unmatched in presidential history.
Nothing illegal, there's nothing wrong with it.
